## MKCinema 1.4: offline downloads, and torrents on Mac and Linux

| Platform | File | Requirements |
|---|---|---|
| Android phones and tablets | `MKCinema.apk` (app 1.4.0) | Android 7 or later |
| Android TV, Google TV, Fire TV | `MKCinema-TV.apk` (the same file) | Android TV 7 or later |
| Windows | `MKCinema.exe` (app 1.3.0) | Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit, Microsoft Edge WebView2 |
| macOS | `MKCinema-1.1-mac.zip` (app 1.1) | macOS 11 or later, Intel and Apple silicon |
| Linux | `mkcinema_1.1_amd64.deb` or `mkcinema-1.1-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` (app 1.1) | x86-64, WebKitGTK 4.1 (2.40 or newer) |
| LG webOS (beta) | `com.mkcinema.app_1.1.0_all.ipk` | unchanged |

The Android app installs over 1.3.0 and keeps your sign-in. The Windows app has no installer: replace the old `MKCinema.exe`.

### Offline downloads (Android phones and tablets, Windows)

- A **Download** button on film and episode pages, and **Library › Downloads** to play or delete what you've saved.
- **Android**: downloads keep going with the app closed and show in the notification shade. They're saved in the app's own folder, so no storage permission is needed. **Wi-Fi only** is on by default. With no internet, the app opens straight to your downloads. The phone player now has touch controls.
- **Windows**: files go to `Videos\MKCinema`, two at a time, and resume after a dropped connection. Subtitles are saved next to the film for VLC.
- Not offered on TVs.

### Torrents on Mac and Linux (1.1)

- **Settings › Desktop app**, off by default, with the same download-only engine as Windows and Android. It never uploads or seeds, and the pieces are deleted when it's turned off or the app closes. Settings explains that peers can see your IP before it can be turned on.
- On Mac, MKV files may not play inside the app: use the IINA or VLC hand-off.

### Mac

The Mac app is now a `.zip`. Safari unzips it into Downloads; drag **MKCinema** into **Applications**. It isn't notarized, so open it once, then go to **System Settings › Privacy & Security › Open Anyway**.

The Windows exe isn't code-signed yet, so the first run shows "Windows protected your PC": choose **More info**, then **Run anyway**.

See [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/itbelikethatbruh/MKCinema/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) for the web app changes, which every app gets automatically.

**Fire TV:** in Downloader, enter `mkctv.pages.dev`.
